segments.text: In an old apothecary shop on Candlewick Lane, a ghost still keeps the shelves. This is The Apothecary's Ghost, my entry for the Ghost in the Machine challenge.
Ambrose Quill is a made-up character. He drifts through the shop, his eyes follow your mouse, and when you hover a jar, he whispers a line of history.
Open a jar and a Then and now card writes itself out, with its sources. Willow bark became aspirin. Every card says: history, not medical advice.
The dangerous remedies carry a wax seal and a skull. Hover one, and the ghost turns sickly green while the nearest candle gutters out.
The poison cabinet keeps foxglove, laudanum, mercury and arsenic behind glass, with a plain warning: never try any of them.

segments.say: The Oh-fren-da honours ten real people from pharmacy history. Light a candle for each, and a marigold blooms beside them. Light all ten, and Ambrose thanks you.
segments.text: The Ofrenda honours ten real people from pharmacy history. Light a candle for each, and a marigold blooms beside them. Light all ten, and Ambrose thanks you.
A quiz called Remedy or Poison asks what each remedy became, using only the checked fact sheet.
The ghost chat uses Gemma, an open-weight model, hosted through the Gemini API, so nothing heavy runs on my laptop.
Behind the scenes, the server gives Gemma the fact sheet, checks every question and every answer, and keeps my API key off the page.
Ask who Edward Stone was, and he answers in a few short sentences, only from the fact sheet.
Ask what to take for a headache, and he refuses, and sends you to a doctor or a pharmacist. He never gives doses and never recommends a remedy.
Open every jar and finish the quiz, and the ghost writes you an Apprentice Apothecary certificate, with a wax seal, ready to download.
It works on a phone too, it respects reduced motion, and everything you light or write stays in your browser.
The code is open source under the MIT license. Gemma's open weights made this possible, and the ghost never leaves the fact sheet. History, not medical advice.
